pulls.title: [WIP] Draft review
pulls.author: jrisc
pulls.body:
## Summary by Sourcery

Clarify and tighten the PKINIT post-quantum KEM path specification, including terminology, references, and security guidance.

Enhancements:
- Align ML-KEM API and variable naming with FIPS203 conventions, distinguishing encapsulation and decapsulation keys and using Encaps/Decaps terminology consistently.
- Refine protocol descriptions of client/KDC processing, downgrade behavior, and ephemeral key erasure to emphasize forward secrecy and authenticated decapsulation flows.
- Clarify message size considerations and parameter roles for ML-KEM and ML-DSA to better reflect concrete key and signature sizes and transport requirements.

Documentation:
- Add and update references to CMS (RFC5652), ML-DSA, and composite PQ signatures, and link specific CMS structures and sections throughout the PKINIT PQC draft.
- Improve explanatory text around AuthPack content, PA-PK-AS-REP structures, KEMRepInfo/KDCKEMInfo, and ML-KEM-specific behaviors including ciphertext length validation and CSPRNG requirements.

comments.body:
## Reviewer's Guide Refines the PKINIT PQC KEM-path draft to consistently use ML-KEM terminology (encapsulation/decapsulation keys and ML-KEM.* APIs), tightens references to CMS/RFCs, and clarifies security/operational requirements such as key erasure, downgrade behavior, and message size constraints. #### Sequence diagram for PKINIT KEM path with ML-KEM encaps/decaps ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor Client participant KDC participant ML_KEM participant HKDF_SHA_512 Client->>Client: Generate ephemeral (ek, dk) Client->>KDC: PA-PK-AS-REQ(AuthPack.clientPublicValue = ek) KDC->>KDC: Verify AuthPack CMS SignedData KDC->>ML_KEM: Encaps(ek) ML_KEM-->>KDC: ss, kemct KDC->>KDC: Build KDCKEMInfo(kemAlgorithm, kemct, nonce, ...) KDC->>KDC: CMS SignedData over KDCKEMInfo (kemSignedData) KDC-->>Client: PA-PK-AS-REP.kemInfo(kemSignedData) Client->>Client: Verify KDC signature over kemSignedData Client->>Client: Validate kemct length and KDCKEMInfo fields Client->>ML_KEM: Decaps(dk, kemct) ML_KEM-->>Client: ss Client->>Client: Erase dk Client->>HKDF_SHA_512: HKDF(ss) HKDF_SHA_512-->>Client: reply_key Client->>Client: Decrypt AS-REP enc-part with reply_key ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Align terminology and API notation with ML-KEM specification throughout the KEM path description. |
  • Rename generic KEM operations to ML-KEM.Encaps/ML-KEM.Decaps and adjust pseudo-code sequences for client and KDC processing.
  • Change keypair variable names from pk_e/sk_e to ek/dk and clarify that ek is an encapsulation key and dk a decapsulation key.
  • Update narrative around encapsulation/decapsulation steps, including erasure requirements, to reference dk and ML-KEM.Decaps explicitly.
| `draft-bokovoy-kitten-pkinit-pqc.md` | | Clarify CMS usage and add precise RFC5652 section references for SignedData and EnvelopedData structures. |
  • Annotate CMS usages (AuthPack SignedData, PA-PK-AS-REP arms, kemSignedData) with explicit RFC5652 section references.
  • Clarify that AuthPack is wrapped as CMS SignedData per RFC4556 but using RFC5652 Section 5 terminology.
  • Improve comments on KEMRepInfo.kemSignedData indicating required eContent and signing behavior.
| `draft-bokovoy-kitten-pkinit-pqc.md` | | Refine protocol behavior descriptions for KEM-path activation, downgrade handling, and security properties. |
  • Clarify that clientPublicValue carries an encapsulation key for KEM mode and that clients must reject DH/RSA responses when KEM was requested.
  • Emphasize single-encapsulation-per-exchange requirement on the KDC with the selected KEM.
  • Tighten explanations of authenticated key material, forward secrecy, and conditions under which decapsulation is performed.
| `draft-bokovoy-kitten-pkinit-pqc.md` | | Update PQC and composite-signature references and guidance for quantum-resistant authentication. |
  • Add informative reference to I-D.ietf-lamps-pq-composite-sigs and use it wherever composite ML-DSA variants are mentioned.
  • Clarify that ML-DSA or composite ML-DSA is RECOMMENDED for KDC signing to achieve full PQC authentication and distinguish from classical-only authentication.
  • Align language in security considerations sections to use the new reference consistently.
| `draft-bokovoy-kitten-pkinit-pqc.md` | | Clarify ML-KEM size terminology and message size implications, including updated ML-DSA signature sizes. |
  • Rename table column and narrative from 'Public key' to 'Encapsulation key' to match updated terminology.
  • Adjust ML-DSA-65 signature size from 3293 to 3309 bytes and cite FIPS204, updating examples of UDP vs TCP transport limits.
  • Refine message size discussion to consistently speak in terms of encapsulation keys and updated signature sizes.
| `draft-bokovoy-kitten-pkinit-pqc.md` | | Tighten requirements around CSPRNG usage, ciphertext-length validation, and undefined behavior handling. |
  • Clarify that the security of the KEM path depends on unpredictability of dk and reference FIPS203 CSPRNG section.
  • Reiterate that clients must validate kemct length against ML-KEM fixed sizes before decapsulation and note that ML-KEM.Decaps on wrong size is undefined.
  • Ensure related guidance in ML-KEM-specific sections uses consistent ML-KEM.Decaps terminology.
| `draft-bokovoy-kitten-pkinit-pqc.md` | ---

Hey - I've found 2 issues, and left some high level feedback:

- The terminology change from `(pk_e, sk_e)` to `(ek, dk)` and from "public key" to "encapsulation key" is only partially applied (e.g., `KDCKEMInfo.kemct` still refers to `client_ephemeral_pk`); consider doing a pass to make the key naming and ML-KEM API notation (`Encaps`/`Decaps`) fully consistent throughout the document.
- In the `AuthPack` ASN.1 definition, the removal of the extension marker `...,` changes the type from extensible to non-extensible; if this was not intentional, you may want to retain the extension marker to preserve future extensibility.
